title: Payroll roster and terminations, January to June 2026
what_it_shows: 7 active employees by role: the pharmacist-owner, 1 staff pharmacist, 1 Store Manager (registered pharmacy technician), 1 lead pharmacy technician, 1 pharmacy technician, 1 front-store clerk and 1 delivery driver; 1 termination in the period, a pharmacy technician with a last working day in late April 2026; payroll runs biweekly; no employee health plan deductions

title: PMS user and role list
what_it_shows: 8 active named accounts mapped to 4 roles (pharmacist, technician, clerk, administrator); only the pharmacist role can verify prescriptions; the Store Manager holds the administrator role and the pharmacist-owner is the backup administrator; no shared or generic accounts

title: PMS security settings
what_it_shows: MFA required only for web sign-in from outside the store; the store network is set as a trusted location, so in-store sign-in uses a password only; idle sessions end after 60 minutes, changed from the 15-minute default at the store's request in 2019 (settings history); password rule is the vendor default of 8 characters; accounts lock after repeated failed sign-ins; the audit trail records user, patient, action and time

title: PMS workflow settings and EPCS audit report queue
what_it_shows: A pharmacist must verify every prescription entered and filled by a technician; the daily EPCS audit report is generated each business day; the report queue keeps 90 days of reports and all 90 are marked unopened

title: PDMP submission log, June 2026
what_it_shows: The PMS generated and sent a controlled substance reporting file to the Florida PDMP each night in June 2026, with no manual step

title: Productivity suite users, authentication and audit settings
what_it_shows: 8 named user accounts, each with MFA enforced (on since 2025) by push approval with number matching off, including the administrator account; lockout after failed sign-ins on vendor defaults; audit logging on, kept for the plan's default period of less than one year; automatic external forwarding allowed; no alert rules for mass downloads or new forwarding rules

title: Productivity suite BAA status
what_it_shows: The vendor's business associate agreement shows as accepted in 2024; a saved copy is filed in the BAA folder

title: Cloud fax portal user list

title: Shared-drive folder and permission report
what_it_shows: Folders restricted by group; HR files limited to the Store Manager and the pharmacist-owner; contents include monthly delivery log exports since 2021 (names, addresses, prescription numbers), ALF order sheets and medication lists, packaging schedules, controlled substance inventory spreadsheets, invoices and HR files; the drive is synced to the store desktops by the suite sync client

title: Mail encryption settings

title: MSP device list

what_it_shows: 7 managed computers: 5 desktops (2 intake stations, 1 pharmacist verification station, 1 pickup counter station with a signature pad, 1 back-office desktop) and 2 laptops (pharmacist-owner, Store Manager); the packaging controller workstation appears only as an exclusion from patching and antivirus, noted as at the equipment vendor's request, with an operating system version past its vendor support end date; the delivery phone appears only in the MSP's mobile device settings; no network devices or SaaS services listed

title: MSP device policy report
source_system: MSP remote monitoring and management console
what_it_shows: 10-minute screen lock on the 2 laptops and the back-office desktop; the 3 counter desktops sign in automatically to one shared operating system account and are excluded from the screen lock policy

title: MSP encryption report
source_system: MSP remote monitoring and management console
what_it_shows: Full-disk encryption on the 2 laptops; not enabled on the 5 desktops; the packaging workstation listed as not encrypted; the delivery phone reports built-in encryption with a passcode; the laptops and the phone can be wiped remotely

title: MSP monthly service report, June 2026
source_system: MSP report emailed to the Store Manager
what_it_shows: Monthly OS and application patching of the 7 managed computers; firewall firmware updated quarterly; antivirus on the 7 computers; the packaging workstation listed as excluded from patching and antivirus at the equipment vendor's request; services listed do not include vulnerability scanning or endpoint detection and response

title: Antivirus console export
what_it_shows: Antivirus active on the 5 desktops and 2 laptops with automatic definition updates, real-time scanning, weekly full scans and quarantine; no agent on the packaging workstation; alerts go to the MSP help desk queue, which is staffed in business hours; no alert is sent to the pharmacy

title: Firewall, Wi-Fi and network configuration export
source_system: MSP network documentation and firewall management
what_it_shows: The firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and exposes no services; one internal staff network holds the desktops, the packaging workstation, the VoIP phones and the camera recorder; staff Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with one shared password, last changed in 2021 according to the MSP's network notes; guest Wi-Fi is a separate network with internet access only; firmware updated quarterly

title: Backup job report and settings, April to June 2026
source_system: Cloud backup console (SYS-07), exported by the MSP
what_it_shows: Nightly copy of the shared drive and nightly images of the back-office desktop and the packaging workstation; 30 days of versions; immutable retention off; one MSP administrator account; no restore jobs in the job history

title: MSP ticket history, January 2024 to June 2026
what_it_shows: A 2024 ticket closes the retirement of one desktop with no wipe or destruction record attached; reimage tickets before computers were reused, with no wipe record attached; no restore test tickets

title: Packaging workstation remote-support settings
source_system: Packaging controller workstation (SYS-05), viewed with the Lead Pharmacy Technician
what_it_shows: The equipment vendor's remote-support tool runs at all times and accepts unattended connections with one shared vendor password; no session log is kept on the workstation; the packaging software uses one shared packaging login

title: BAA and contracts folder
what_it_shows: Signed BAAs with the PMS vendor (since 2019), the MSP (since 2021) and the cloud fax vendor, and the saved acceptance of the productivity suite BAA (2024); no BAA with the packaging equipment vendor or the proof-of-delivery app vendor; the MSP BAA requires the MSP to hold BAAs with its subcontractors; no MSP subcontractor list or backup vendor BAA in the folder; no EPCS third-party audit report in the folder; no arrangements with governmental entities; the folder is kept on paper only

title: PMS vendor agreement
what_it_shows: Hosted PMS since 2019 with the vendor's backups and disaster recovery; e-prescriptions including EPCS, real-time retail pharmacy drug claims to PBMs through a claims switch using the NCPDP Telecommunication Standard, and the nightly PDMP file are carried by the vendor under its own subcontractor agreements; audit records kept for the contract term; no recovery time or recovery point figures in the agreement

title: PMS vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report
what_it_shows: Type 2 report with an unqualified opinion for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31, covering security, availability and confidentiality; 1 exception (2 of 40 sampled releases deployed without documented approval, remediated 2026-02); the system description states an RTO of 4 hours and an RPO of 30 minutes, encryption of stored data and customer incident notice within 72 hours; complementary user entity controls listed; hosting provider, claims switch and e-prescribing network carved out

title: PMS vendor EPCS product statement
what_it_shows: The vendor states that the PMS meets the DEA application requirements for electronic prescriptions for controlled substances and has a third-party audit; the audit report is available on request and was not among the documents on file

title: PMS release notes, May 2026
what_it_shows: The release notes for the vendor's May 2026 release are marked unread; the release adds a controlled substance risk score, switched on by default for all user roles and shown as a Low, Elevated or High flag on each incoming controlled substance prescription

title: Controlled substance risk score documentation
what_it_shows: Score from 0 to 100 shown as Low, Elevated or High with the top three contributing factors; inputs are patient age and sex, prescriber and pharmacy counts, morphine milligram equivalents, early refill history, payment type and patient-to-prescriber distance; no PDMP data; trained on de-identified dispensing data from the vendor's customer base; no validation or subgroup performance data published

title: PMS drug utilization review configuration
what_it_shows: Rule-based interaction, allergy, duplicate therapy, and age- and sex-based dosing and pregnancy alerts from a licensed drug knowledge base; the pharmacist resolves each alert before verification

title: MSP service contract
what_it_shows: Covers help desk, patching, antivirus, firewall, Wi-Fi and backup administration; describes the remote management tool that reaches every store computer; 4-business-hour response time; no recovery time commitment; no incident notice timeframe; no subcontractor list; the cloud backup subscription is resold by the MSP

title: Packaging equipment service contract
what_it_shows: Supply and service of the strip packager and its controller workstation; next-business-day on-site support; remote support by the vendor's support team; no recovery commitment for the workstation software; no business associate terms

title: Store card statements and vendor invoices, July 2025 to June 2026
source_system: Store credit card statements; vendor invoices
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the PMS vendor, the productivity suite vendor, the cloud fax vendor, the MSP (monthly service including a resold backup subscription), the packaging equipment vendor, the internet provider, the phone carrier, the mobile carrier for the delivery phone, the payroll service, the accounting SaaS, the card processor and the cyber insurer; invoices from the drug wholesaler; no charges from the proof-of-delivery app vendor, from AI tool vendors or from a training vendor

title: Internet and phone service agreements
source_system: Store Manager's contracts folder; carrier invoices
what_it_shows: One business internet line with no second line or failover; the VoIP phones use the same line; the main number can be forwarded to a cell phone

title: ALF management company supply agreement
what_it_shows: Weekly adherence packs and deliveries for residents of two assisted living facilities run by one management company

title: ALF management company security questionnaire
what_it_shows: Security questionnaire organized by the Trust Services Criteria, received in July 2026; response due 2026-09-30; the instructions accept a self-assessment from small vendors

title: Payer, PBM and Medicaid enrollment files
what_it_shows: Florida Medicaid provider enrollment; PBM network agreements covering Medicare Part D and commercial plans; claims submitted in real time through the claims switch; no federal contracts

title: Licenses, registrations and certificates
source_system: Store files (framed permit and registration; DEA certificate records)
what_it_shows: Florida community pharmacy permit naming the pharmacist-owner as prescription department manager; DEA registration as a retail pharmacy for Schedules II to V; one CSOS certificate, issued to the pharmacist-owner; services offered are retail prescriptions, delivery and adherence packaging, with no compounding, immunizations or substance use disorder treatment

title: Cyber liability insurance policy
what_it_shows: Policy in force since the 2024 renewal with a 24x7 breach hotline and panel breach counsel and forensics; the policy requires prompt notice before outside firms are hired

title: SaaS vendor security documentation
source_system: Vendor websites and portals (productivity suite, cloud fax, backup vendor through the MSP)
what_it_shows: The productivity suite, cloud fax and backup vendors describe encryption of stored data and TLS for data in transit

title: Policies folder and document request response
source_system: Policy binder in the back office; document request list
what_it_shows: A purchased 2019 policy binder with no adoption date, approval signature, tailoring or review record; the request for a risk analysis, an incident response plan or incident procedure, an EPCS incident reporting procedure, a contingency plan, downtime procedures, a contact list, a records retention schedule and an incident log returned none other than the 2022 checklist (EV-039)

title: 2022 PMS vendor HIPAA checklist
what_it_shows: Yes/no checklist supplied by the PMS vendor; no likelihood or impact ratings; no later risk analysis was provided

title: Privacy and Security Officer designation letter
what_it_shows: Letter signed by the pharmacist-owner on 2026-07-10 naming the Store Manager HIPAA Privacy Officer and Security Officer

title: HIPAA privacy video sign-in sheet
what_it_shows: All 7 staff signed after watching the HIPAA privacy video at hire; the video dates from 2019 and covers privacy; no security training, refresher, reminders or phishing exercises are recorded

title: Employee handbook
what_it_shows: Covers conduct and cash handling; no HIPAA or security sanctions rule

title: Independent assessment engagement letter
what_it_shows: Fixed-fee engagement of an independent HIPAA security consultant for a control assessment in August 2026

title: FY2025 sales and cash report
what_it_shows: Sales of about $1.1 million across about 306 business days, about $3,600 per business day; cash reserve covers about 3 weeks of expenses; the wholesaler is paid weekly

title: Dispensing, patient and delivery volume report, Q2 2026
what_it_shows: About 3,100 active patients; about 55 prescriptions a business day, about 12% controlled substances and about 7% cash; about 70 adherence pack patients, including about 40 residents of two ALFs; about 25 deliveries a day; records for about 11,500 individuals since 2012; all patients served at one Florida store

title: Key and alarm code list
what_it_shows: Keys and alarm codes for the monitored burglar alarm held by the pharmacist-owner, the Staff Pharmacist and the Store Manager; the technician who left in April 2026 held no key, alarm code or store device

title: Store walk-through and equipment count
what_it_shows: 5 desktops, 2 laptops, 1 delivery phone, and the strip packager with its controller workstation in the packaging room counted; firewall, Wi-Fi equipment and the camera recorder on the back-office network shelf; VoIP phones; a locked Schedule II safe in the prescription department; cameras over the counter and the safe; keyed store entry with an alarm keypad; no backup generator; a standalone card terminal at the register; one storefront

title: Intake interview: systems, data and store processes
what_it_shows: The Store Manager adds and removes accounts when remembered, with no checklist and no access review, and uses the PMS administrator account for daily work; ePHI is held in the PMS, email and the shared drive, the fax portal, the delivery app, the packaging workstation and downloaded faxes in the counter desktops' download folders; the delivery app driver login was set up for the previous driver and passed to the current driver in 2025 without a password change; the packaging login is shared by the 3 people who build packs; vendor notices, including PMS release notes, go to the Store Manager's email; no incident log is kept

title: Staff AI tool survey
what_it_shows: Staff report seeing a colored flag (Low, Elevated, High) on incoming controlled substance prescriptions since the May 2026 PMS release, including technicians and the front-store clerk; responses mention public generative AI chatbots used to draft letters or answer questions; the survey did not record how many staff use them or what was entered; no list of approved AI tools exists in the documents provided

title: BIA interviews with process owners
source_system: Interviews (pharmacist-owner, Staff Pharmacist, Store Manager, Lead Pharmacy Technician, MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: Each owner's description of their process, the systems, vendors and people it uses, its manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss they say it can tolerate; adherence packs are built 2 days before the Wednesday delivery; the wholesaler delivers next day and fast movers are stocked for about 2 days; a nearby independent pharmacy has agreed informally to accept transferred prescriptions and lend stock during outages; none of the workarounds is written down

title: Risk analysis interviews
source_system: Interviews (pharmacist-owner, Staff Pharmacist, Store Manager, Lead Pharmacy Technician, Delivery Driver, MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: Owners' accounts of past events and near misses; staff describe approving MFA push prompts without checking them and sending faxes to new numbers without a second check; the Lead Pharmacy Technician states past claims switch outages lasted hours; the MSP lead technician states its remote management console requires MFA and reaches every computer, with no supporting evidence supplied; the Delivery Driver uses the one shared app login

title: Account comparison, 2026-07-14
source_system: Payroll terminations (EV-001) compared with the PMS and suite user lists; PMS and suite sign-in logs
what_it_shows: The pharmacy technician who left in late April 2026 still had active PMS and suite accounts, about 11 weeks after the last day; sign-in logs show no use after the last day; both accounts were disabled on 2026-07-14

title: Gap analysis interviews
source_system: Interviews (all 7 staff and the MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: Owners' descriptions of how each HIPAA safeguard and DEA duty is carried out today. The pharmacist-owner (2026-07-14) states the pharmacy sponsors no group health plan, no sanction has ever been recorded, and nobody has asked the PMS vendor for its EPCS audit report; staff state nobody reviews PMS reports or suite sign-ins, no security reminders are sent, and they have not read the policy binder; the pharmacists describe emergency refills, PDMP outage rules, transfers and duplicate-prescription checks done case by case with no written step; counter staff often keep working under the last person's open PMS session; vendor technicians are escorted by a pharmacist; there is no procedure for entering the store after a storm or alarm event, no record of lock, alarm or camera repairs and no retention rule for security records; the Lead Pharmacy Technician describes a fax with an ALF resident's medication list sent to a wrong number in March 2026, handled by phone and not assessed or logged; the MSP lead technician states the backup console login uses a password only and that no restore test record exists

title: Store walk-through (physical safeguards), 2026-07-15
what_it_shows: Keyed store entry with a monitored alarm; cameras over the counter and the Schedule II safe; the safe locked; the prescription department closed to the public; the pickup counter screen faces the waiting line; the 3 counter desktops stay signed in to the shared account and do not lock; the packaging workstation stays signed in to the shared packaging login

title: PMS permission report, 2026-07-16
what_it_shows: The permission to annotate and alter dispensed controlled substance prescription records is held by the 2 pharmacists, the Lead Pharmacy Technician and the Store Manager; the change history shows it was given to the 2 non-pharmacists in 2019 to fix claim errors

title: PMS role change and alteration audit trail review, 2026-07-17
source_system: PMS admin console and audit trail (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The alteration permission was removed from the Lead Pharmacy Technician and the Store Manager on 2026-07-17 and the role list now shows it on the pharmacist role only; the pharmacist-owner's review of 12 months of alterations found claim corrections and no change to a drug, quantity or patient

title: Owner laptop and Schedule II ordering check, 2026-07-16
source_system: Owner laptop browser; wholesaler order history; Store Manager interview
what_it_shows: The CSOS certificate password was saved in the owner laptop browser; the Store Manager places Schedule II orders on the owner laptop with the pharmacist-owner's certificate; the wholesaler order history shows no order the pharmacist-owner did not recognize

title: CSOS certificate revocation confirmation, 2026-07-17
what_it_shows: Revocation of the pharmacist-owner's CSOS certificate requested and confirmed on 2026-07-17; Schedule II orders to use paper DEA order forms until a new certificate is issued

title: EPCS audit report review, 2026-07-21
source_system: PMS EPCS audit report queue (90 retained reports)
what_it_shows: All 90 retained daily reports opened for the first time: 4 failed sign-ins and the alteration events by the 2 non-pharmacists (claim corrections); the review note records that none was judged a security incident

title: EPCS record sample and retrieval test, 2026-07-21
what_it_shows: In the 10 sampled records the pharmacists annotated in the PMS annotation fields and the dispenser fields came from the signed-in user; records kept since 2019 were retrieved by patient, prescriber, drug and date

title: Sample of emails to the ALFs, July 2026

what_it_shows: 4 of 10 sampled emails to the ALFs containing medication lists were sent without the encrypt option

title: Personnel file review
what_it_shows: Pharmacist and technician licenses and registrations checked on the state license lookup at hire; each application asks the DEA employee screening question

title: BAA terms review
what_it_shows: The 4 BAAs on file are vendor templates; the PMS vendor BAA says security incidents are reported promptly, covers its e-prescribing, claims switch and PDMP subcontractors and permits de-identification; the MSP BAA says within 30 days and requires subcontractor BAAs; no terms with the packaging equipment vendor or the delivery app vendor

title: CSOS replacement certificate record
what_it_shows: A new CSOS certificate issued to the pharmacist-owner on 2026-08-03; paper DEA order forms used from 2026-07-17 to 2026-08-03; the certificate password is not saved in the browser

title: PMS vendor EPCS third-party audit report
what_it_shows: Third-party audit by a Certified Information Systems Auditor dated 2025-10-15 stating that the PMS meets the pharmacy application requirements, with no limitation on additional prescription information; the pharmacist-owner recorded the 21 CFR 1311.200(a) determination on 2026-08-12

title: Controlled substance risk score review, 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-19
source_system: PMS controlled substance prescriptions, 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-31 (342), with the pharmacists' documented assessments
what_it_shows: 342 prescriptions: 41 flagged High, of which the reviewing pharmacist agreed on 22; 34 judged by pharmacists to need extra steps, 3 of them flagged Low; 3 refusals and 5 delays, 2 delays started by a technician because of the flag; High-flag rates of 9% for women and 15% for men, 24% under 30 and 5% at 65 and older, 31% cash and 10% insured; the score display was limited to the pharmacist role on 2026-08-19

title: Control assessment: account management test
source_system: PMS, suite, fax portal and delivery app user lists compared with the staff roster; termination record; Store Manager and MSP lead technician interviews
what_it_shows: Account types, approvals, creation and removal steps are not documented and accounts have never been reviewed; account requests are approved verbally; the delivery app has one shared driver login used since 2025; the counter desktop and packaging passwords were not changed when the former technician left; PMS roles match job duties for all 7 users after the 2026-07-17 change; the pharmacist role is granted only after license verification

title: Control assessment: personnel termination review
source_system: Termination record for the former technician; key and alarm code list; Store Manager interview
what_it_shows: No time limit set for disabling access; the former technician's accounts stayed active about 11 weeks; MFA registrations and the shared counter and packaging passwords were not changed; no exit discussion of confidentiality; the former technician held no keys or devices and returned the name badge; records created by departed users are kept in the PMS

title: Control assessment: least privilege review
source_system: PMS role list and permission report (2026-08-05); counter desktop account settings
what_it_shows: Controlled substance alteration limited to the pharmacist role; the shared counter desktop account has local administrator rights; the Store Manager uses the PMS administrator role for daily work

title: Control assessment: audit review interview and log check
source_system: PMS EPCS audit report screen and review log; suite audit log; pharmacist interviews
what_it_shows: The daily EPCS audit report was never opened before 2026-07-21; from 2026-07-21 to 2026-08-04 it was reviewed on 5 of 13 business days, with no log; no defined recipient for findings and no step for the one-business-day report to DEA and the PMS vendor; PMS access reports and suite sign-ins are not reviewed

title: Control assessment: administrator MFA sign-in tests
source_system: Sign-in attempts to the backup console and to the PMS administrator role inside the store, with the MSP lead technician
what_it_shows: The backup console accepted a password alone; the PMS administrator role signed in inside the store with a password alone; suite administrator accounts use MFA

title: Control assessment: malicious code protection test
source_system: MSP antivirus console export; harmless test file on the back-office desktop; after-hours test alert
what_it_shows: Antivirus on the 5 desktops and 2 laptops with automatic updates, weekly full scans and real-time scanning; none on the packaging workstation; the test file was detected on download and quarantined; an after-hours test alert on 2026-08-05 was not seen by the MSP until 8:40 a.m. the next day; nothing reaches the pharmacy; one false positive in 2026 resolved the same day by MSP ticket

title: Control assessment: backup configuration review
source_system: MSP backup job report (July 2026) and retention settings; PMS vendor SOC 2 report; MSP lead technician interview
what_it_shows: PMS data backed up by the vendor; the July 2026 job report shows nightly shared-drive copies and images of the back-office desktop and the packaging workstation; backup copies encrypted; versions not immutable; 30 days of versions; the console accepts a password alone; security documentation (BAAs, designation letter) kept on paper only; firewall configuration backup not confirmed

title: Control assessment: contingency test review
source_system: MSP confirmation of restore history; Store Manager and MSP lead technician interviews
what_it_shows: No contingency plan or test criteria exist; no restore has ever been done, as the MSP confirmed

title: Control assessment: training records and staff interviews
source_system: Video sign-in sheet; interviews with 5 of 7 staff
what_it_shows: All 7 staff watched the privacy video at hire; no security training at hire or after, no refresher, no reminders or phishing simulations; the video dates from 2019; no training after the 2026 PMS release; the March 2026 misdirected fax was not used for training

title: Control assessment: vendor agreement review
source_system: BAA folder; vendor list; MSP contract; PMS vendor SOC 2 and EPCS audit reports; packaging and delivery app vendor terms
what_it_shows: The PMS vendor supplies a SOC 2 Type 2 report and an EPCS third-party audit report; the packaging equipment vendor connects at any time without approval or a session record and has no BAA; the delivery app holds patient names and addresses on free-tier terms with no BAA and unknown retention; no MSP security review; the MSP technician list and backup subcontractor BAA confirmation requested on 2026-07-28 were not received by fieldwork end; the MSP contract, BAAs and draft SSP define who does what

title: Control assessment: encryption test
source_system: Encryption status on 2 desktops (intake station and pickup counter station) and the Store Manager laptop
what_it_shows: Both desktops unencrypted, each with downloaded faxes in the download folder; the Store Manager laptop encrypted

title: Control assessment: staff reporting interviews
source_system: Incident records (none); draft POL-03; interviews with 5 of 7 staff
what_it_shows: No reporting rule or time limit in use; 4 of 5 staff interviewed did not know whom to call after hours; the March 2026 misdirected fax was not reported; no defined recipients for incident information; POL-03 was a draft

title: Control assessment: risk assessment documents
source_system: P01 risk register and report (draft); 2022 vendor checklist; pharmacist-owner interview
what_it_shows: 2026 risk analysis completed 2026-07-24 with SP 800-30 tables, covering all 9 systems and impact on patients; reviewed with the pharmacist-owner on 2026-07-28 and shared with the Staff Pharmacist and the MSP lead technician; the earlier document is a 2022 vendor checklist; the annual update rule is in a draft policy only

title: Control assessment: patch review and test
source_system: MSP patch report (July 2026) and patch policy; patch status on the packaging workstation, 1 counter desktop and the back-office desktop; firewall firmware record
what_it_shows: The MSP scans the 7 computers monthly for missing patches and reports monthly to the Store Manager; updates run on MSP test machines for one week before release; the July report shows 2 desktops 34 days behind on a critical update; the packaging workstation runs an unsupported operating system and is excluded from patching at the equipment vendor's request, with no approval or change record; firewall firmware applied with no recorded test; no update time limits defined

title: Control assessment: authenticator review and test
source_system: PMS and suite password settings; local administrator password tried on 3 computers (MSP present); owner laptop browser; Wi-Fi record
what_it_shows: The same local administrator password worked on 3 of 3 computers tried, and the MSP confirmed it is set on all 5 desktops and the packaging workstation (since 2021); the PMS password rule is 8 characters; the packaging vendor support password is the one set at installation; staff Wi-Fi password unchanged since 2021; no procedure for lost or compromised authenticators; accounts issued in person with temporary passwords changed at first sign-in; laptops and the delivery phone require a PIN or passcode
